method: One dossier per saved watchlist ticker (35, read from cra.watchlist on the live dashboard) plus the curated ideas and the mega-caps carried from the book — 49 in total. p is the Jul 17 close from stockanalysis.com. buy ~4% below the close; stop by type (core -11%, value -10%, momentum -12%, speculative -18% from buy); sell ~18% above buy (~30% speculative). Conviction is capped at 3 for negative-net-income and story names and the reason is flagged in bear[]. stockanalysis.com's fundamentals API returned 404 this run, so analyst targets were unavailable and percentage rules were used for sell levels.

OKTA.why: Identity is the control plane for AI agents; carried an Overweight/$171 call into the week.
bull: Agent identity is a genuinely new TAM
OKTA.thesis: Dropped from the curated list this week on software weakness, but retained in the book.

LYFT.why: Fell 2.9% Friday; the number-two ride-hailing asset with an autonomy option.
LYFT.thesis: A cheap option on autonomy, not a compounding business.

XOM.why: Rose ~1% while the S&P fell 1% — Brent $88.10 and a Hormuz blockade.
bear: $88 Brent already prices a lot of war premium
XOM.thesis: The most liquid way to own the geopolitical bid. Implied growth 15.5% flatters a commodity business at a cyclical high.

SLB.why: Reported on Jul 17; services lag refiners badly in this particular oil shock.
bear: Removed from the book this week — refiners are the better expression
Oil at $88 has not translated into service pricing
SLB.thesis: The wrong end of the energy complex right now.

JPM.why: Fell only 0.6% in a 1% down tape — the quality bid is intact.

NOW.why: Removed from the book this week as enterprise software kept de-rating.
bull: Workflow platform with real switching costs
NOW.thesis: Good business, hostile tape for the category.

MU.why: HBM is the tightest link in the AI chain, but memory was the weakest corner of the tape.
bull: HBM sold out well into next year
bear: SK Hynix and SanDisk fell ~7% last week
Deeply cyclical — the cycle turns without warning
MU.thesis: Highest-beta way to be long AI hardware, in both directions.

FISV.why: Fell 2.1% Friday; a director bought FIS in the same beaten-up group on Jul 15.
bear: Payments has been a value trap all year
FISV.thesis: Cheap for a reason, but insiders in the group are starting to buy.

SYM.why: Fell 1.7%; robotics with real customer concentration risk.

MSFT.why: Most defensible of the big AI spenders; $72.9B TTM FCF.
bear: Hyperscalers now punished for capex, not rewarded
MSFT.thesis: Implied growth 17.1% — demanding but not absurd for this franchise.

MELI.why: Fell 2.3% with growth names; dropped from curated ideas but kept in the book.
bear: Credit book losses in any downturn
MELI.thesis: The best non-US growth asset in the book.

HTZ.why: $1.80 and -3.7% Friday. This is a balance-sheet situation, not a business.
bull: Any refinancing would re-rate the equity
bear: Balance sheet is the entire story — conviction capped at 2
Equity could be wiped in a restructuring
HTZ.thesis: Scored F on the worst-of list. Own it only as a lottery ticket.

GS.why: Gave back 5% after a blowout print — conviction cut from 4 to 3 on that reversal.
bull: Blowout Q2 already in the books
bear: Gave back the entire earnings pop within a session
GS.thesis: When a stock cannot hold a good print, the tape is telling you something.

FSLR.why: Flat Friday; removed from the book as power exposure consolidated into GEV/VST/CEG.
bear: Removed from the book this week
FSLR.thesis: Kept on the watchlist rather than the book.

ETN.why: Electrification arms dealer across grid, data centre and industrial.
ETN.thesis: The least exciting and most durable way to own the power build.

VST.why: Merchant power as the cleanest expression of AI electricity demand.
bear: Power names are a crowded trade
VST.thesis: Dropped from curated ideas this week purely on crowding, not thesis.

OSCR.why: Rose 0.8% Friday in a sector where Elevance insiders were buying.
bear: Unprofitable and policy-dependent — conviction capped at 2
OSCR.thesis: The speculative version of the Elevance trade.

NVDA.why: Rep. Cleo Fields disclosed three buys at $192.53; the stock closed Jul 17 at $202.81.
bull: $119.1B TTM FCF and a net cash balance sheet
bear: The whole chip complex is de-rating on AI-capex doubt
Any hyperscaler capex trim hits estimates first
NVDA.thesis: Implied growth 17.5%. The price is not the problem; the narrative is.

NFLX.why: Fell 7.3% Friday to $68.95, against a 52-week high of $128. Conviction cut to 2.
bear: Down ~46% from its 52-week high — conviction cut to 2
NFLX.thesis: A falling knife until it holds a level.

NCLH.why: Fell on Friday; fuel at $88 Brent is a direct cost headwind.
NCLH.thesis: The wrong side of the oil trade.

CRWD.why: Held up better than software peers, down only 0.3%.
bear: Implied growth 34.2% — the highest in the reverse-DCF by far
CRWD.thesis: Excellent company, demanding price. The DCF is the bear case.

CCJ.why: Fell ~2% Friday, which improves the entry on an intact long-term contracting cycle.
bull: Tier-1 supply plus the Westinghouse stake
Nuclear build-out is a decade-long demand story
CCJ.thesis: Conviction held at 4. Weakness here is opportunity, not information.

VRT.why: Fell 1.6% with the AI complex; the physical bottleneck, not the silicon.
bear: Trades with the chip complex regardless of fundamentals
VRT.thesis: Sold off with semis despite a different business model.

SOFI.why: Fell slightly Friday; a rate-cut-sensitive consumer lender.
bear: Consumer credit quality is the risk
Rate cuts now less certain with oil at $88
SOFI.thesis: Oil-driven inflation is a direct headwind to the rate-cut thesis.

SMCI.why: $24.18 and -2.0%. Scored C on the worst-of list.
bull: Cheap on forward numbers if they are real
bear: Full exposure to the AI-capex doubt
SMCI.thesis: Highest-risk way to be long AI servers.

LULU.why: Fell 2.1% to $116.33; a broken growth story trading as value.
LULU.thesis: Value only if the brand thesis holds.

UA.why: Rose 2.7% to $7.28. Scored D on the worst-of list.
bear: Brand still unfixed after years of resets — conviction capped at 2

OPEN.why: $4.50 and -1.5%. Scored F on the worst-of list.
bear: Inventory model breaks in a slow housing tape — conviction capped at 2

ASML.why: Fell with the group; the EUV chokepoint and the best leading indicator in semis.
bull: Order book leads the whole wafer-fab equipment cycle
bear: Semicap de-rates violently on any capex doubt
ASML.thesis: Dropped from curated ideas this week on group weakness, kept in the book. Implied growth 24.2%.

CEG.why: Largest US nuclear fleet; the utility that trades like a growth stock.
bear: Priced for a great deal of AI demand
CEG.thesis: If AI power demand is real, this is the purest listed expression. If it is not, this is an expensive utility.

SMR.why: $7.72, +1.1%. Pre-revenue, and Decisive Point's $19.1M into Standard Nuclear shows the theme still attracts capital.
bear: Pre-revenue and cash-burning — conviction capped at 3
SMR.thesis: The option, not the business. BWXT is the version with revenue.

TE.why: $5.84 and -1.7%. Scored D on the worst-of list.
bear: Cash burn against a hostile policy backdrop — conviction capped at 2
Execution risk on the capacity ramp

CRWV.why: $73.21, +0.4%. Directly exposed to the hyperscaler-capex question now being asked.
bear: Heavy debt-funded capex — conviction capped at 3
Excluded from reverse-DCF on negative FCF
CRWV.thesis: The purest expression of the thing the market is currently doubting.

APLD.why: $25.79 and -2.5%. Leases capacity to AI tenants.
bear: Balance sheet is stretched — conviction capped at 2
Financing risk if capex sentiment sours further
APLD.thesis: Levered to exactly the debate that broke the tape this week.

NBIS.why: $177.71, +3.5% — one of the few AI-adjacent names up on Friday.
bear: Negative FCF — conviction capped at 3, excluded from reverse-DCF
NBIS.thesis: Relative strength on a bad day is worth noting.

VLO.why: Record 3-2-1 crack spreads and up 3.1% on a day the S&P fell 1%.
bull: Nymex 3-2-1 crack hit a record $64.58/bbl on Jul 8
Refining margins have nearly tripled in 2026
Up more than 80% YTD and still making highs
bear: A Hormuz de-escalation compresses the whole trade
VLO.thesis: The Gulf war made refined products scarce, not crude. Valero converts that scarcity into cash faster than any producer, and reverse-DCF puts its implied growth at just 8.9% — the lowest in the book.

MPC.why: Largest US refiner; +2.2% Friday, +80% YTD on the same crack-spread engine.
bull: MPLX midstream cash flow underpins the dividend
$5.7B TTM FCF against a $312 share price
bear: Margin cycle can roll over in a quarter
MPC.thesis: Same trade as Valero with more leverage — both operating and financial. Implied growth 9.1%.

JEF.why: Sumitomo Mitsui bought $318.7M of stock at $53.96 on Jul 15, lifting its stake +222%.
bull: SMFG now holds 8,566,379 shares and gets a board seat
Largest single insider print of the week across the whole market
bear: Purchase price adjusts over a two-month reference period
Smaller and more volatile than GS or JPM
JEF.thesis: When a strategic partner buys a fifth of a billion dollars of stock in the open market and takes a board seat, that is a different signal from a director buying $20,000.

ELV.why: CEO bought ~$1.0M and a director bought $366K — both on Jul 17, same day.
bull: CEO Gail Boudreaux added 2,725 sh at $367.79, +2% to her stake
Director Ramiro Peru bought 1,000 sh at $366.05 the same day
$201.1B TTM revenue against a ~$80B market cap
bear: Managed care has been broken all year on medical cost trend
Insurer accounting — excluded from the reverse-DCF
ELV.thesis: Same-day buying by the CEO and a board member in a sector everyone has given up on is the classic setup. It is also the classic value trap, so size it small.

CAVA.why: Traffic-led comps and best-in-class unit economics — rare in restaurants right now.
bull: New-unit returns among the best in the group
Comps driven by traffic, not price
CAVA.thesis: A genuine unit-growth story that has nothing to do with AI or oil — useful diversification when leadership is this narrow.

ANET.why: Flat on Friday while the semis around it fell 4.5% — relative strength worth noting.
bull: Ethernet displacing InfiniBand in AI back-ends
bear: Premium multiple in a de-rating group
ANET.thesis: If the AI trade survives in a narrower form, the network is the last piece to get cut. Implied growth 16.5% is modest for the quality.

BWXT.why: Naval reactors and SMR components — revenue today, not a 2032 story.
bull: Defence budget insulation from the cycle
BWXT.thesis: The nuclear theme without the pre-revenue risk. Decisive Point's $19.1M buy into Standard Nuclear on Jul 16 says capital is still flowing into the fuel cycle.

GEV.why: Gas turbines are sold out for years — the genuine bottleneck in adding generation.
bull: Turbine slots booked into the late 2020s
bear: Very high expectations embedded in the price
GEV.thesis: You cannot build a data centre without power, and you cannot build power without turbines. The constraint is physical.

EQT.why: Rep. Thomas Kean Jr bought Jun 1 at $55.26; the stock closed Jul 17 at $49.56, below his fill.
EQT.thesis: Gas is the swing fuel for data-centre load. Buying below where a disclosed congressional buyer filled is a reasonable place to start.

NTSK.why: Two 10% holders each bought ~$3.77M at $12.29 on Jul 10 — an unusually clean cluster.
bull: Iconiq and director Griffith each bought 306,399 sh
NTSK.thesis: The cleanest two-buyer insider cluster in the book, but it is a story stock until the P&L says otherwise.

AMZN.why: Fell 1.1%; Rep. Crenshaw disclosed a sale at $261.26.
bull: Advertising is now a major profit pool
bear: TTM FCF is negative on capex — excluded from the reverse-DCF
AMZN.thesis: The capex question applies here more than anywhere.

AVGO.why: Custom accelerators and networking — the less headline-sensitive leg of AI infra.
bull: Custom XPU pipeline across multiple hyperscalers
bear: $64.9B total debt turns net cash sharply negative
AVGO.thesis: Implied growth 21.9%, and the debt raises that bar.

GOOGL.why: Fell 4.6% on Jul 16; Rep. Crenshaw sold at $372.58.
bear: Implied growth 23.9% is the second-highest among the mega-caps
Search disruption risk from AI answers
GOOGL.thesis: Largest cash cushion in the group, highest bar among the mega-caps.

LLY.why: The largest earnings engine in large-cap pharma.
bear: Implied growth 28.8% — capacity capex suppresses current FCF
Compounding and pricing pressure on incretins
